section: 2. Two layers and one question: where does the control signal enter?
text: **Sensor level (64 papers).** The families are defined by the signal: ego action or trajectory (19), layout, box, map or BEV conditioning (16), unified multi-condition control (16), text or language (4), inference-time guidance or editing (3), prediction without a control input (2), other (2), camera or viewpoint (1) and scenario, risk or event conditioning (1). 20 of the 64 are from 2024, 23 from 2025 and 17 from 2026.
previous_sentence: **Scenario level (77 papers).** Trained-in conditioning is the largest family (18), then inference-time guidance (17), language or LLM-driven methods (13), other methods such as black-box adversarial search (11), models with no steering signal kept for contrast (7), reinforcement-learning fine-tuning (5), latent-space control (3) and reward or return conditioning (3). 32 of the 77 papers are from 2026 and 18 from 2025.

section: 2. Two layers and one question: where does the control signal enter?
text: The two layers share the same injection mechanisms (cross-attention, adaptive normalisation, a ControlNet-style branch, token conditioning, guidance at sampling time) but differ in what the signal means: a risk level, a goal point or a language clause at the scenario level; an ego pose, a box layout or a weather prompt at the sensor level.
